claim: Double-shot injection moulding creates permanent keycap legends by moulding the legend symbol in plastic during a first step before moulding the surrounding keycap body around it in a second step.
excerpt: Double-shot moulding is a two-step process. In the first step, the legend or graphics to be placed on the keycap, are moulded in plastic. The plastic insert, resulting from the first step, is then placed into another mould, and plastic is inserted under heat to combine both moulds to a single piece keycap.

claim: Double-shot moulding requires individual physical moulds for each unique legend and row profile, leading to high tooling costs compared to post-mould legend printing.
excerpt: the process of building moulds for each and every legend is an expensive process compared to making one mould per row profile and adding the legends afterwards on demand, especially considering manufacture for the wider international market where even simple letters such as "A" move between row profiles

claim: Dye-sublimation heat-infuses dye into the plastic matrix rather than painting a top layer, but requires dye pigments that are darker than the base plastic.
excerpt: whereas dye sublimation causes the dye to sink into the plastic... this means that you cannot use dye sublimation to print white lettering (as nothing is brighter than white) or to print onto black keycaps (as nothing is darker than black).

claim: Reverse dye-sublimation produces light-colored legends on dark keycaps by dying the entire keycap surface while preserving the natural light plastic color for the legend.
excerpt: In reverse dyesub, the entire keycap except the legend is dyed, leaving the legend as the same color as the keycap base.

claim: Pad printing transfers ink onto keycap surfaces using flexible pads, offering low cost and material versatility but poor wear resistance over time.
excerpt: Pad printing has been the most popular form of keycap printing since the 1990s, which uses pads dipped into ink to transfer lettering onto the keycaps. Pad printed legends are known for a lack of durability.

claim: Laser marking alters or burns keycap material to render fine line legends, but experiences difficulty creating uniform coverage across solid filled legend areas.
excerpt: Laser marking is the use of a laser beam to mark the legends onto the keycaps. Laser marking works well with straight lines, but has difficulty achieving clean coverage of solid fill areas such as arrowheads.

claim: European ISO keyboards contain one extra key relative to ANSI layouts and swap the right Alt key for AltGr to allow access to third-level typographic characters.
excerpt: In addition to having one extra key, the ISO layout has another fundamental property: the right Alt key is replaced with the Alt Gr key, which is a typographic meta key that accesses the third symbol on a keyboard.

claim: Enthusiast group buys supply European regional layout variations through modular add-on kits covering UK, German QWERTZ, and Nordic legends.

claim: The standard South Korean Dubeolsik keyboard layout arranges consonants on the left keys and vowels on the right keys.

source.title: Difference Between Korean and Japanese - Nexvirox

excerpt: Korean uses a 2-set Dubeolsik keyboard layout, mapping consonants and vowels to separate keys.

claim: Japanese input on modern computers predominantly uses Romaji phonetic entry on standard QWERTY letter keys.
excerpt: The whole concept of Wāpuro rōmaji (ワープロローマ字) revolves around using a qwerty keyboard with Roman letters to input Japanese characters.

claim: Cangjie input relies on character visual shape breakdown rather than phonetic pronunciation like Zhuyin or Pinyin.
excerpt: Cangjie works based on the shape of the characters, rather than the sound of the characters like pinyin or zhuyin.

claim: The standard keyboard layout for Cyrillic script input across Russian and Eastern European keyboards is JCUKEN.
excerpt: The Russian JCUKEN layout is used for typing in Cyrillic script.

claim: Dye-sublimation achieves high wear resistance because pigment penetrates into the plastic substrate rather than sitting on the keycap surface.

source.title: Mechanical Keyboard Materials & Sound Guide - KBDfans

excerpt: Because the dye penetrates the plastic, the legend is highly wear-resistant. Standard dye-sub works best with darker legends on lighter keycaps.

claim: Pad printing is the dominant industrial method for mass-produced commercial keyboard legends worldwide.
excerpt: Pad printing now accounts for virtually all commercial (office and consumer) legend printing across the world.

claim: In right-to-left layout contexts, coordinate space and visual layout orientation place the origin at the upper-right corner.
excerpt: In right-to-left (RTL) applications, the upper-right corner is the origin.
